title: Selection, Not Fusion: Radar-Modulated State Space Models for Radar-Camera Depth Estimation
claim: Injecting the secondary modality inside the sequence operator's selection parameters, with resolution-dependent fusion, replaces external feature fusion at linear cost.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right pipeline plus zoomed block detail, color-coded modality arrows
description: Two dashed-border panels. Panel (a), the SemoDepth pipeline, has two rows. The top row takes an RGB road photo through a blue Image Encoder into a pyramid of shrinking blue slabs labeled c0 to c4. The bottom row takes a radar point cloud, drawn as teal dots in a cloud, through a teal Radar GSE block. Teal arrows labeled r0 to r4 rise from the GSE and meet blue arrows coming down from the image features. The two meet at fusion blocks L0 to L4, which are grouped into Tier 1 (FiLM), Tier 2 (windowed RMS) and Tier 3 (4-dir RMS). These feed a Head block and then a green Depth block. Panel (b) zooms into the RMS block. Blue x_img and teal x_rad boxes connect to colored circles A, B, Δ and C. Teal arrows show radar entering Δ and C, and blue arrows feed B. These circles lead into a State Update Block that holds the discretization and recurrence equations, and then into a Readout Block that computes y_t. The eye goes first to the colorful pipeline, then to the teal and blue contrast in panel (b).
caption: SemoDepth architecture. (a) Pipeline. A ResNet-34 image encoder and a radar graph structure extractor (GSE) built on PCA-GM produce the image pyramid c0, . . . , c4 and one radar feature map. Projections (1×1) of this map at each level form the radar pyramid r0, . . . , r4. MVSP allocates fusion by resolution. FiLM modulates the two finest levels (Tier 1). Windowed RMS around each projected radar return serves the middle level (Tier 2). RMS over the full image in four directions serves the two coarsest levels (Tier 3). (b) Radar-Modulated Selection (RMS). Radar adds modulations to the step size ∆t and readout Ct (teal arrows). The input projection Bt is computed from the image only (blue arrows), and the state matrix A never sees radar. The state update block applies zero order hold (ZOH) discretization and the recurrence ht = ¯Atht−1 + ¯Btxt. The readout block emits yt = C⊤
abstract: Radar camera depth estimation turns a very sparse but metric radar signal into a dense depth map. Existing methods combine radar and image features outside the sequence operator of the backbone, through concatenation, confidence gating, sparse supervision, or graph based extraction. Mamba variants for multimodal fusion also leave the selection mechanism itself unimodal. We argue that selection is the right place for radar to enter. We introduce Radar-Modulated Selection (RMS), which injects radar inside the selective scan of Mamba. Radar adds learned perturbations, initialised at zero, to the step size $Î$ and the readout $\mathbf{C}$. The input projection $\mathbf{B}$ and the state matrix $\mathbf{A}$ never see radar. At initialisation the block equals a pretrained image Mamba, so radar gains influence only where it improves accuracy. The construction also couples the two modalities at linear cost and falls back to the image backbone when radar is missing. We deploy RMS in a Multi-View Scan Pyramid (MVSP) that matches the fusion operator to the reach of radar at each scale. On nuScenes, SemoDepth reduces MAE by 34.0%, 29.9%, and 29.9% over the previous best within 50, 70, and 80 m. It also has the lowest single frame latency among methods with a public release (26.8 ms). A feature blend placed before the scan adds no accuracy on top of RMS, which supports the view that selection inside the scan can replace fusion outside it. When twice as many spurious radar returns as true ones are injected, the MAE@80 of SemoDepth rises by 1.4%, against 33.6% for a Mamba baseline that fuses radar before the scan.
